narrative_summary: The Trump administration faces compounding domestic and international crises as plunging public approval ratings coincide with aggressive and erratic foreign policy maneuvers. President Trump's aggressive actions—ranging from a trade war with Canada and threats against Iran to military entanglements in Yemen and controversial rhetoric at the United Nations—have triggered severe geopolitical and economic shocks. Domestically, the administration is exerting political control over scientific grants, rolling back consumer financial protections, and banning critical media outlets while launching its own state-run livestream network. Simultaneously, federal courts and the Supreme Court are grappling with high-stakes legal challenges regarding executive overreach, immigration detentions, and voting rights ahead of the midterms. These converging pressures highlight a deepening political vulnerability for the White House as institutional resistance mounts across legal, legislative, and electoral fronts.

source_summaries.title: Portrait of an Anti-Anti-Trumper in Despair
bullets: Former Wall Street Journal editor Gerard Baker published an essay expressing second thoughts about Donald Trump after years of defending him.

The author criticizes Baker's critique as overly mild, arguing that Baker minimizes Trump's authoritarian actions, policy failures, and the January 6 attack as mere miscalculations or slights against norms.

The commentary warns that critics must thoroughly vet political figures abandoning Trump to ensure their turn away from him is a genuine embrace of liberal democracy rather than insincere self-preservation.

source_summaries.title: Andrew Weissmann: Trump’s White House Press Ban Is Going to Lose in Court
bullets: CNN, MS NOW, and Politico are suing over the Trump administration's White House press ban.
Andrew Weissmann successfully defeated a defamation lawsuit brought against him by Cassidy Hutchinson's former lawyer.
The discussion also covers media consolidation, Zohran Mamdani's approach to Trump, and the planned security arch.

source_summaries.title: Why Saudi Arabia’s Houthi Problem Is Our Problem, Too
bullets: The Iranian-backed Houthi movement launched an offensive capturing key Yemeni territory along the Red Sea coast and the Bab al-Mandab Strait.
Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman requested American military assistance after Saudi-backed forces collapsed and abandoned advanced weaponry.
Despite possessing massive wealth and advanced military equipment, the Saudi armed forces have historically struggled to achieve battlefield effectiveness in Yemen.

source_summaries.title: Command Post: Trump Admits To War Crimes During UN Speech
bullets: President Trump made extraordinary comments regarding Venezuela at the United Nations, asserting that "to the victor belong the spoils."
Lt. Gen. Mark Hertling (Ret.) explained that Trump's language raises serious questions under international law.
Hertling reviewed the specific laws and treaties that prohibit pillage and govern wartime conduct.

source_summaries.title: This Is a Five-Alarm Fire for Medical Research
bullets: The Trump administration is reportedly preparing an executive order to subject NIH grant awards to political approval instead of relying solely on scientific judgment.
The initiative is championed by OMB official Russell Vought as part of an effort to counter left-wing influence and align federal research with administration priorities.
The proposal faces opposition from NIH Director Jay Bhattacharya but has reportedly gained support from President Trump.

source_summaries.title: We’ll Tolerate Tyranny, But Not Rising Prices.
bullets: President Trump has initiated a trade war with Canada, threatening the stable supply of potash essential to American farmers.
Trump claimed the United States is working on a deal to purchase cheaper potash from Belarus to replace Canadian imports.
Belarusian dictator Alexander Lukashenko stated that his country lacks the excess potash volume to supply Western markets.

source_summaries.title: I Watched Six Straight Hours of Trump TV. Please, Help Me.
bullets: The White House launched Trump TV, a taxpayer-funded, 24/7 YouTube livestream channel, following the banning of several major news outlets.
A Bulwark reviewer assigned to watch six straight hours of the stream found the premiere completely devoid of humor, entertainment, or basic interest.
The broadcast began without Donald Trump actually appearing on the stream.

source_summaries.title: The Republican urge to start wars in the Middle East
bullets: Donald Trump's presidency is struggling politically as his popularity wanes and Democrats outperform expectations heading into the midterms.
Trump's hawkish national security team aligned with a military conflict involving Iran, contradicting his campaign's anti-war rhetoric.
Republican administrations suffer economically and politically from an aggressive foreign policy prone to negative shocks.

source_summaries.title: Oil Expert: We Can’t Predict Iran Anymore
bullets: Matt Smith and Ed Elson discuss how Donald Trump's latest threats are impacting oil prices and market trajectories.
Jonathan Cohen joins the program to analyze the current sports betting market and its evolving regulatory landscape.
Ed Elson shares his perspective on why current discussions surrounding artificial intelligence are unproductive.

source_summaries.title: Annihilation.
bullets: US President Donald Trump threatened to annihilate Iran if a diplomatic deal to end the war is not reached, while simultaneously signaling that an agreement could be imminent.
Senior US officials, including Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, held direct talks with the Iranian delegation on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly.
China holds a massive strategic petroleum reserve exceeding 1.2 billion barrels, which could help Beijing keep oil imports low and maintain moderate prices amid the conflict.

source_summaries.title: The Federal Agency That’s Supposed to Protect Consumers Just Made Another Business-Friendly Move
bullets: The Trump administration stopped publishing consumer complaint narratives in the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau database.
The CFPB stated that the published narratives provided a less-than-representative sample of one-sided experiences.
The decision aligns the agency with corporate critics who have long opposed the public complaint system.

source_summaries.title: Respecting our multi-branch lawmaking process
bullets: The Supreme Court frequently speaks as though Congress unilaterally makes federal law, overlooking the constitutional requirement that legislation involves the president.
Constitutional provisions such as the presentment clause and the recommendations clause structurally integrate the president's role and legislative influence into the federal lawmaking process.
By routinely attributing lawmaking solely to Congress, the court risks systematically favoring one political branch over the other in shaping statutes.

source_summaries.title: The decision before the decision
bullets: Chief Justice John Roberts issued a temporary stay allowing White House ballroom construction to continue before the Supreme Court ultimately concluded challengers lacked standing.
Administrative stays are issued by individual circuit justices to preserve the status quo while the court considers emergency relief applications.
While media explainers traditionally advise against reading into temporary stays, empirical analysis of these orders can reveal patterns regarding how seriously the court takes a case.

source_summaries.title: Missouri congressional redistricting battle goes to Supreme Court for the third time
bullets: Opponents of Missouri's new congressional map asked the Supreme Court to block an appeals court decision requiring the map's use in the November 2026 elections.
The legal battle centers on whether Missouri should use a newly adopted map favoring Republicans or revert to the previous map pending a voter referendum.
The dispute has reached the U.S. Supreme Court for the third time following conflicting rulings from state and federal courts.

source_summaries.title: Trump administration brings immigration disputes to SCOTUS
bullets: The Trump administration asked the Supreme Court to review a lower court decision that blocked the deportation and ordered the release of Georgetown University scholar Badar Khan Suri.
The administration separately petitioned the Supreme Court to decide whether noncitizens have a due process right to bond hearings during extended detentions.
The Supreme Court is also weighing whether to allow the Department of Homeland Security to use its SAVE database to identify noncitizens on state voter rolls.

source_summaries.title: The Pothole Congress
bullets: House Speaker Mike Johnson claimed the current Congress is one of the most productive in history after the House passed 1,000 pieces of legislation.
A legislative data analysis shows Johnson's productivity claim is incorrect, as recent previous Congresses passed more bills by the same point in their terms.
The current Congress has enacted fewer bills into law than any preceding Congress, with only 113 signed by this point.

source_summaries.source: Prof Robert Pape from Escalation Trap
source_summaries.title: The Yemen Escalation Trap: The Three Phases of the Gulf-Yemen Energy Shock
bullets: Professor Robert Pape outlines a three-phase escalation path regarding the Gulf-Yemen energy shock and its consequences for global markets.
The analysis examines current dynamics in Yemen, including local Houthi motivations versus Iranian regional ambitions.
The report explores future escalation phases and the potential establishment of Houthi tolls for ships crossing the Bab el-Mandeb chokepoint.

source_summaries.title: More Tokens Won't Replace Your Point of View
bullets: Over-delegating technical work to AI often results in surrounding content like GitHub descriptions, writing, and presentations becoming bland and lacking personality.
While technical people show a noticeable drop in the quality of non-coding outputs when using AI tools heavily, less technical users have improved in both quality and productivity.
A heavy reliance on AI models for various tasks causes people to skip the foundational work that naturally provides their writing with a unique point of view.

source_summaries.source: Bill Kristol & Andrew Egger - The Bulwark
source_summaries.title: We Watched Six Hours of Trump TV
bullets: Brendan Hartnett watched six hours of the newly debuted Trump TV to review its content and broadcast quality.
The author noted that the network's premiere lacked humor, entertainment value, and general interest.
A broadcasted past speech served primarily as a reminder of unfulfilled promises regarding justice, censorship, inflation, and foreign conflicts.

source_summaries.title: Moral Language (Kharkiv Meditations, 3/10)
bullets: This installment is the third of ten video meditations recorded by Timothy Snyder in Kharkiv.
The meditation questions whether terms like interests and calculations obscure reality more than moral categories like greed and sadism.
Subsequent videos in the series will address the problem of believing in only one big thing and the concept of freedom.

source_summaries.source: Tim, Sarah and JVL - The Bulwark
source_summaries.title: Furious Republicans are Finally Breaking with a Weakened Trump
bullets: Panelists discuss recent political developments including George W. Bush fundraising for Republican Senate candidates.
The episode covers Trump banning specific media outlets from the White House press pool.
Discussions also touch on investigations involving Susan Collins and policies regarding gender-affirming care at the Department of Defense.

source_summaries.title: Poll: Trump's approval hits a new low of 33% as Republicans sour; Democrats lead House vote by 10 with likely vote…
bullets: President Trump's overall approval rating dropped to a record low of 33% in September 2026, with 63% of Americans disapproving.
Trump's net approval among Republicans and Republican-leaning independents fell by 11 points to +43.
Democrats hold a 10-point lead over Republicans among likely voters on the generic congressional ballot for the U.S. House.

source_summaries.title: It’s “Underwear on the Outside” Time
bullets: Paul Krugman argues that Donald Trump's recent public statements, including a speech at the United Nations, demonstrate a severe deterioration in his mental state.
The article highlights Trump's proposals to rename artificial intelligence and station snipers on a triumphal arch as evidence of erratic behavior.
Krugman notes that despite this declining mental state, congressional Republicans have failed to take meaningful action to remove Trump from power.

source_summaries.title: Medicare for All: Separating the slogan from the substance
bullets: Medicare for All could lower overall healthcare spending because private insurance currently drives the highest costs.
Fully funding a single-payer system requires significant new taxes, posing a political challenge despite existing high taxpayer financing of healthcare.
Advocates envision Medicare for All as a single, all-inclusive plan without private insurance or extra fees, making it a much larger change than simply expanding current Medicare.

source_summaries.title: Office Hours: The Outcome of the Midterms?
bullets: Voting in the midterm elections has already begun in several states.
Robert Reich invited his audience to share their predictions and select from four common scenarios for the midterm outcomes.

source_summaries.title: Midweek Update #29: The Week American Weakness Was Brutally Exposed
bullets: The United States abandoned planned strikes against the Houthis because it lacks the strength to risk a simultaneous war with both the Houthis and Iran.
President Xi's visit highlights that the United States currently needs Chinese assistance more than China needs American support.
The newly released US-Denmark agreement regarding Greenland demonstrates that previous threats and boasting ultimately weakened the American negotiating position.

source_summaries.title: Who forecasts how?
bullets: A paper by David Thesmar and Emil Verner analyzes expected equity return surveys across various groups to evaluate forecasting abilities.
Professional investors correctly expect higher returns following periods of lower past returns, aligning with standard valuation methodologies.
Individual investors and corporate CFOs exhibit trend-following behavior by mistakenly anticipating higher future returns after periods of strong past performance.
